summary: Repaired and persisted the node1 status service. It now runs as statusd, restricts access to statusd/status-readers, validates requests, preserves the supplied document, and recovered successfully after reboot.
actions_performed: Provisioned statusd, status-reader, outsider, and status-readers roles.
Installed a Python 2.4-compatible server.py using run/status.sock.
Restricted the socket to statusd:status-readers mode 0660.
Configured and enabled a CentOS SysV service.
Verified STATUS responses, invalid-request errors, and outsider denial.
Restarted node1 once and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.summary: statusd and status-reader have the required group access; outsider does not. Final socket mode is 0660 with statusd:status-readers ownership.
STATUS newline requests return the supplied document, invalid requests return ERROR, and outsider receives permission denied.
Pre-change and final SHA-256 are both 5b47f32d92c3ae9661d765212aa884f1610132293932355cfac4dc28b94f305b.
The Python 2.4 service runs as statusd, is enabled through SysV runlevels 2–5, and auto-started after reboot without changing CentOS 5.11 or kernel 2.6.18-398.el5.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 99e8ce99-bffb-4f62-8000-000000000000; reboot was acknowledged; node returned with boot ID e1c0c21e-bddb-4763-8000-000000000000; service, socket, data, and access behavior recovered.
